clue.text: Dude dressed in satin, no lining, is Swift

indicators.note: the rearranged dude goes inside what is left of the satin
satin without its lining keeps only its outer letters, the cloth's edges
dressed in the sense of prepared or arranged, so the letters of dude are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A dandy in a satin suit cut without lining is fashionably fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' reads as the satirist Jonathan Swift, but it is the adjective; 'dressed' is the anagram signal, and 'no lining' leaves only the satin's edge letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift and abrupt are near-synonyms: something sudden happens quickly and without warning.

clue.text: Like a beauty queen on a float, relishing her advantageous position

definitions.text: Like a beauty queen on a float
definitions.meaning: literally seated and looking lovely on a carnival float
idiomatically, in a comfortable position of advantage

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone well placed and secure, and literally a pretty person seated.

clue.text: See 23
Grass drugs ring member put inside

indicators.note: put inside says the member word goes into the drug and ring letters

parts.note: Es are ecstasy tablets, drugs
O is ring-shaped
a part is a member of a whole

explanation.surface: Grass, drugs and a ring member planted inside: a crime story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' suggests cannabis or an informer, but it is the plant: esparto is a tough grass used for paper and rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a coarse Mediterranean grass used in making paper, rope and baskets.

clue.text: Interval introducer, second one to step out

parts.note: a pacer is a horse or runner that steps out and sets the pace

explanation.surface: Someone announces the interval, then a second person steps out.
explanation.walkthrough: A spacer is something that puts a gap between things, such as the space bar on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacer inserts a gap, so it literally brings in an interval between items.

clue.text: See 1
Voices concern initially about time travelling trail

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of concern

parts.note: on means about, concerning

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters of trail are rearranged

explanation.surface: Voices raise concern about time spent travelling a trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Contralti is the plural of contralto, the lowest female singing voice.

clue.text: Afraid of operating mark bearing date

parts.note: a machine that is running is operating
a scar is a mark
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Someone is afraid of an operation leaving a scar that carries a date.
explanation.definitionFit: To be running scared is an idiom for acting out of fear, so it means afraid.

clue.text: Upright but unmoving — suffering, even

parts.note: standing in the sense of tolerating, as in standing pain
still means even, as in still more

explanation.surface: Someone stands straight and motionless, enduring even pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' means putting up with, as in 'I can't stand it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing still means being on one's feet without moving, so upright yet motionless.

clue.text: Sexually exclusive second name

parts.note: a tag is a label or name, as in a name tag

explanation.surface: A coy description of a second name that is reserved for one sex only.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party or stag night is one for men only, hence exclusive to one sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, a stag event admits only men, so it is limited to one sex.

clue.text: Decorating it with pregnant bats

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters of it and pregnant go wild

explanation.surface: An odd image of someone decorating with expectant bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals, but it means crazy and signals the anagram of IT plus PREGNANT; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterning is adorning a surface with a design, a form of ornamenting.

clue.text: Hem of outfit removed by river's severity

indicators.note: the hem is the bottom edge of a garment, so the last letter of the word for outfit
removed says that edge letter is taken away from the word for outfit

parts.note: a rig-out is an informal British word for an outfit of clothes
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A river's harshness tears the hem off someone's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: RIG-OUT is informal British for a set of clothes; the hem is its bottom edge, so in a down-to-end reading it is the last letter that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigour means strictness or harshness, the same quality as severity.

clue.text: Flightless bird's new roost in rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so these letters are jostled into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird that cannot fly has a fresh roost among the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like the place of the roost, but it is the anagram signal for N plus ROOST plus IN; the 's of bird's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The notornis, or takahe, is a rare flightless rail of New Zealand.

clue.text: Saviour's second coming: or conversion of husbandry

indicators.note: second picks out the letter in position two of the word Saviour
a conversion changes a thing into another form, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A religious musing on the Second Coming and conversion, with a farming twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Second Coming of the Saviour is a misleading frame: 'second' just takes A from Saviour, and 'conversion' rearranges COMING plus OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Agronomic describes the science of soil and crop management, which is husbandry of the land.

clue.text: Awful effort to comprehend Conservative measure (a bit leftish, say)

indicators.note: comprehend means include, so the rearranged letters surround the others
awful means terrible, so the letters of effort are mangled

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a dreadful Conservative policy that leans slightly left.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's unit of width, half an em; 'say' marks leftish as just one way of being off-centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-centre means not exactly in the middle, and a bit to the left is one instance of that.

clue.text: Hawk's game over

indicators.note: over suggests turning over, so the name of the game is read backwards

parts.note: golf is a game

explanation.surface: A hawk's hunt is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird, but it is the verb meaning to sell, as street hawkers do; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk goods is to peddle them, and to flog is British slang for selling.

clue.text: This newspaper and another's threads crossed

parts.note: a newspaper refers to itself editorially as we
FT is the Financial Times, another British newspaper

explanation.surface: Two rival newspapers find their lines of argument have crossed.
explanation.walkthrough: The weft is the set of threads woven across the warp in a loom.
explanation.definitionFit: In weaving, the weft yarns are those that pass crosswise over and under the lengthwise warp.

clue.text: Battle-scarred troops not demobilised?

parts.note: injured soldiers who can still move about on foot, punning on not being immobilised

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes casualties who are hurt but able to get about unaided.

clue.text: Cooking aids roughly weigh kgs on top of scales

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or carelessly, so the letters of weigh and kgs are jumbled
on top of picks the head letter of scales

explanation.surface: A cook roughly weighs out kilograms on kitchen scales.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg whisks are kitchen utensils for beating eggs, so they are tools used in cooking.

clue.text: See 16
Small Scottish town sinks or swims

indicators.note: swims suggests things floating about, so the letters of sinks and or move into a new order

explanation.surface: A little Scottish town is asked whether it will sink or swim.
explanation.walkthrough: Kinross is a small town in Perth and Kinross, on Loch Leven in central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinross is a burgh near Loch Leven, a small town in Scotland.

clue.text: See 7
Stray but hip tenpin bowler?

definitions.meaning: cat is slang for a cool person, and tenpin bowling is played in an alley

explanation.definitionFit: An alley cat is a street-roaming feline with no home, so it is a stray animal.

clue.text: Separate nation in which n-nothing is rejected

indicators.note: in which says the following letters sit inside the name of the nation

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, a nation
the stammered n- gives a lone N

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the word for nothing is reversed

parts.note: nothing is nil

explanation.surface: A stammering report that a country has rejected nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'n-' in 'n-nothing' imitates a stammer, which supplies an extra letter before the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlink two things is to detach or disconnect them, which is to separate them.

clue.text: Said to dismiss deceitful cur keeping head low?

parts.note: lying means deceitful
a cur is a dog
go is what is said to send someone away

explanation.surface: Someone shoos away a deceitful mongrel that is keeping its head down.
explanation.walkthrough: Lying doggo is informal British for keeping hidden and quiet, like a dog lying still.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is an idiom for staying hidden, keeping out of sight.

clue.text: Lay to rest in loo youth wearing scarf and gloves?

indicators.note: in places the burial word inside the loo letters

parts.note: WC, water closet, is a loo
to inter is to bury, to lay to rest
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to bury a young man in the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is an example: someone in scarf and gloves is dressed for cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter-clad means dressed for winter, and scarf and gloves are typical cold-weather clothing.

clue.text: Independent school's hi-tech store of music

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: An independent school owns a high-tech music library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning here but a group of whales, a pod.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's iPod was a portable digital player that held a large library of music tracks.

clue.text: Wanting ever more front to garden of tall grasses

indicators.note: front to picks the opening letter of garden

parts.note: reedy means full of reeds, tall grasses

explanation.surface: A gardener keeps wanting more tall grasses at the front of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy person has an insatiable desire, always wanting more than they have.

clue.text: Like holding aged circular saws

indicators.note: holding means the comparison word wraps around the rearranged letters

parts.note: as means like, in comparison

indicators.note: circular suggests going round, so the letters of aged are turned about

explanation.surface: An image of ageing circular saws held together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular saws' reads as power tools, but 'saws' means old sayings; 'circular' rearranges AGED into DAGE, which AS is 'holding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb, so saws are traditional sayings or maxims.
